cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's just told them we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ (2 Corinthians 5:10). So now Paul says he knows what it means to fear the Lord.

cards.question: Paul knows what it means to fear the Lord. So what does he try to do with people?

cards.text: Paul says what he is, is clear to God, and he hopes it's clear to the Corinthians' conscience too. Then he adds that he's NOT commending himself to them again. No sir. Not AGAIN.

cards.question: Instead, Paul gives the Corinthians a reason to be proud of him, so they can answer those who take pride in ___ rather than in the heart.

cards.text: Then Paul says if they are out of their mind, it is for God. Out of your mind for God? Friend, I talk to my oven every morning, and NOBODY has ever accused me of a sound mind.

cards.question: Paul says if we are out of our mind, it is for God. But if we are of sound mind, who is it for?
Paul says what compels him is his fear of what people think.

cards.text: Here's what's really driving him: Christ's love compels him. Paul is convinced that "One died for all, therefore all died."

cards.question: Christ died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for ___ but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

cards.text: So from now on, Paul says, we regard no one according to the flesh. From NOW on, friend. That's a line drawn right through the flour.

cards.question: Paul says that at one time, even Christ was regarded according to the flesh.

cards.text: Then comes the big one: "Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation." Friend, I went into a junk drawer blurry and came out SHARP, so this verse hits me right in the handle.

cards.question: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. So what does Paul say about the old?

cards.text: All this is from God, Paul says, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ. And God isn't done yet.

cards.question: God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men's ___ against them.
God keeps the message of reconciliation to Himself and commits it to no one.
Paul says God has committed the message of reconciliation to us. So what does Paul say we are?

cards.text: Paul says it's "as though God were making His appeal through us." Friend, if God made an appeal through ME, I'd be so nervous my mustache would wave at everybody in the room.

cards.question: Paul pleads with them on behalf of Christ: Be ___ to God.

cards.text: Then Paul packs the whole message into one verse. "God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf," he writes. Read that one slow, friend.

cards.question: God made the One who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf. Why?

answers.text: So in Him we might become the righteousness of God
So in Him we might never face hardship again
So in Him we might receive the riches of the world

cards.text: Paul says he and those with him are God's fellow workers. Fellow workers with GOD? Friend, I've got "cookie stamper" on my résumé and I thought THAT was impressive.

cards.question: Paul and those with him are God's fellow workers. What do they urge the Corinthians not to do with God's grace?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes God's words from Isaiah 49:8: "In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you."

cards.question: Paul says the day of salvation is still a long way off.

cards.text: Not someday. Not after you hit snooze five more times. "Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'If they are out of their mind' never says who 'they' are. A baker could read 'they' as the Corinthians. In 5:13 it is 'we' (Paul and those with him), and the next card switches to 'we' and 'our'.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer 'It has passed away' sounds like the Bible. 'It gets patched up' and 'It stays on the shelf' sound casual and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The second half of 5:17, 'Behold, the new has come!', is never told or asked. Stop 1 ends on the old passing away, so the baker misses the key line about the new.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'Paul pleads with them' uses 'them' with no one named. The question has to say who is being pleaded with.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Paul packs the whole message into one verse' claims that 5:21 sums up the whole message. The text never says this, so the storyteller line adds a fact. The card also has three sentences.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: Paul writes 'we' throughout 5:11-6:2, and the letter is from Paul and Timothy (2 Corinthians 1:1). The cards don't handle this the same way. Some make it just Paul ('he tries to persuade', 'what compels him', 'he's NOT commending himself'). One uses an unclear 'they' (stop 1, card 5). One says 'he and those with him' (stop 2, card 9).
findings.question: When a letter writer says 'we', should Papa Dorin retell it as the writer alone ('Paul'), as the writer and his companions ('Paul and those with him'), or keep 'we' open? The docs cover a speaker who says 'I', but not 'we'.
